ione.host: Opennebula RPC2 (xmlrpc) endpoint. By default it is http://opennebula_IP:2633/RPC2
ione.user: Opennebula admin username. By default it is oneadmin, but you may create new user with admin privilege
ione.group: Grop for new VMs and users. By default it is 1
ione.sched: Opennebula host scheduler rules. For example:{"default": "ID="2""} - all VMs will be placed on host ID=2.{"default": "ID="2" | ID="13""}- the host will be chosen between 2 and 13 according to the scheduler opennebula policy. Read more: https://docs.opennebula.io/6.4/installation_and_configuration/opennebula_services/scheduler.html
ione.sched_ds: Opennebula datastore scheduler rules. For example:{"nvme": "ID="10"""ssd": "ID="11"""hdd": "ID="12"""sata": "ID="13""}- the datastore will be chosen between 10-13 according to the one selected when ordering in the application. Read more: https://docs.opennebula.io/6.4/installation_and_configuration/opennebula_services/scheduler.html

proxmox.host: Proxmox VE API endpoint of any cluster node, https only: https://pve.example.com:8006. One node is enough: the API is cluster-wide.
proxmox.auth_mode: User + password is required for the VNC console (PVE vncwebsocket rejects API tokens). An API token works for everything else.
proxmox.user: PVE user in user@realm form, e.g. nocloud@pve. Needs role with VM.Allocate, VM.Clone, VM.Config.*, VM.PowerMgmt, VM.Snapshot, VM.Console, VM.Audit, Datastore.AllocateSpace, Datastore.Audit, Sys.Audit, Pool.Audit.
proxmox.token_id: API token id in user@realm!tokenname form (Datacenter → Permissions → API Tokens).
proxmox.token_secret: Secret shown once when the token is created.
proxmox.insecure: Skip TLS certificate verification (self-signed PVE certificate). Prefer ca_cert in production.
proxmox.ca_cert: PEM of the CA that signed the PVE certificate.
proxmox.pool: PVE resource pool new VMs are added to (optional).
proxmox.sched: Node placement rules. Keys: default and HCPU (used when plan.meta.highCPU). Value: {"nodes": ["pve1","pve2"], "strategy": "least_used"|"round_robin", "reserve_ram_mb": 2048}. Empty nodes = all online nodes.
proxmox.sched_ds: Storage per drive type as ordered in the app: {"SSD": "local-zfs", "HDD": "nas"}. Storage must exist on the target node and allow images.
proxmox.public_ip_pool: Static public addresses handed out via cloud-init: {"ranges": ["a.b.c.10-a.b.c.50", "x.y.z.0/24"], "gateway": "a.b.c.1", "prefix": 24 (or netmask), "dns": ["1.1.1.1"], "bridge": "vmbr0", "vlan_tag": 0}. Addresses already set in ipconfig of any VM are skipped.
proxmox.private_vnet_tmpl: Private pool, same format as the public one (usually another bridge or vlan_tag).
proxmox.full_clone: Full clone copies the disk (default). Linked clone is faster but the template must stay on the same storage and cannot be deleted.
proxmox.vmid_range: Restrict VMIDs the driver may allocate, e.g. 1000–1999. Empty = /cluster/nextid.
proxmox.suspend_mode: What billing suspend does: hibernate (suspend to disk, default), power off, or pause in RAM.
proxmox.qemu_agent_required: Hide templates without qemu-guest-agent. The agent is needed for real IPs, extra IPs and guest stats.
proxmox.min_drive_size: Per drive type limits in MB, e.g. {"SSD": 10240}. Template disk size is always the lower bound.
